hookOptions: Why does Mumbai crave this one fried snack when it rains?
Mumbai rains are chaotic, but this one snack makes it perfect.
Wet shoes, pouring rain, but you’d still stand in this line.
plan.hook: Wet shoes, pouring rain, but you’d still stand in this line.
plan.title: Mumbai's Ultimate Monsoon Street Food Guide
plan.description: Experience the magic of Mumbai rains through its most iconic street snacks. From sizzling Vada Pav to hot cutting chai, here is how the city celebrates the monsoon.

scenes.visualQuery: rain pouring mumbai street yellow taxi headlights reflection wet road night
scenes.voiceover: Wet shoes, pouring rain, but you’d still stand in this line.

scenes.visualQuery: street vendor frying golden vada pav hot oil steam rising monsoon rain background
scenes.voiceover: There’s nothing like the sizzle of hot Vada Pav while the city gets drenched around you.

scenes.visualQuery: hands pouring hot cutting chai tea glass kettle rainy day mumbai
scenes.voiceover: Pair it with a hot cutting chai, spiced with ginger, to wash down the heat.

scenes.visualQuery: crispy onion pakora bhajia being scooped out of frying pan close up
scenes.voiceover: Or grab a plate of crispy Kanda Bhajias. They are literally made for rainy afternoons.

scenes.visualQuery: happy friends sharing food under umbrella marine drive mumbai rain
scenes.onScreenText: Mumbai hits different in the rain.
scenes.voiceover: It’s not just about the food. It’s how the whole city slows down together.

scenes.visualQuery: pov holding half eaten vada pav green chutney dripping cloudy sea background
scenes.voiceover: What’s your go-to street food when it starts pouring? Tell us below!

review.feedback: The hook is highly sensory and effective, but ensure the visual in Scene 1 immediately shows a long, wet queue to match the 'stand in this line' voiceover. Trim Scene 3 (Chai) and Scene 4 (Bhajias) from 6 seconds to 4 seconds to keep the mid-video pacing from dragging. In Scene 5, the line 'It’s how the whole city slows down together' feels slightly contradictory to Mumbai's fast-paced reputation; consider changing it to 'It's how the city finds comfort together.'
